key_points.point: The document frames the current technological landscape as a 'plague' of 'human fracking' that requires a movement to resist, which accelerationists would view as an attempt to discredit and block technological progress. By characterizing the extraction of attention as 'insidious destruction' and 'sacking and empire,' the authors advocate for a collective 'no' to the current digital platforms. Accelerationists would argue that this framing ignores the transformative potential of these systems and seeks to stifle the innovation that drives societal evolution. The document acknowledges that this resistance might be seen as 'quixotic,' yet it insists on a fundamental shift in how we interact with networked systems.
key_points.verbatim: The problem isnÆt ôphonesö, and it isnÆt ôsocial mediaö. The problem is human fracking, a world-spanning land-grab into human consciousness û which big tech is treating as a vast, unclaimed territory, ripe for sacking and empire.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Resist the extraction of human attention by digital platforms to prevent the commodification of human consciousness.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within skeptic discourse that frames the commodification of human attention by digital platforms as a form of exploitation requiring organized resistance. Encompasses: human fracking, attention economy critique, digital platform resistance.

key_points.point: The authors argue that the 'heedless exploitation' of the human psyche by digital platforms places human survival and flourishing in jeopardy, mirroring the destruction of the external environment. They posit that the stakes are existential because the commodification of attention undermines our ability to care, think, and relate to one another. From a safetyist perspective, this aligns with the concern that AI-driven systems can cause irreversible societal damage by eroding the cognitive foundations of human agency. The document notes that this 'new gold rush' into the inner environment is already causing widespread harm to children and adults.
key_points.verbatim: The stakes are existential. And that is because, rightly understood, our actual human ôattentionö û the thing the frackers want, in the form of our eyes on their screens û is nothing less than our ability to care, our ability to think, our ability to give our minds, time and senses to ourselves, the world and each other.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Protect human attention as a fundamental prerequisite for human flourishing and the prevention of irreversible societal damage.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that prioritizes the protection of human cognitive agency against the extractive practices of digital platforms to prevent irreversible societal degradation. Encompasses: existential risk to human flourishing, cognitive agency, attention commodification.

key_points.point: The authors propose forming broad, cross-partisan coalitions to mobilize a 'movement' against the 'human fracking' of digital platforms, aiming to break out of niche tech-critique. They argue that people across the political spectrum—from 'Maga Republicans' to 'Mamdani progressives'—already share a deep-seated agreement that the current algorithmic attention economy is fundamentally broken. By framing this as a 'politics of human attention' or 'attensity,' they seek to move beyond piecemeal regulation toward a new, unified political subject. The document acknowledges that while this sounds quixotic, historical precedents like the environmental movement show that such shifts can happen rapidly.
key_points.verbatim: The answer is clear: we, the actual people of this planet, must come together in decisive solidarity; we must say no to the human frackers, and do so by insisting, in new ways, that human attention is human, and it is ours, and we will use it to make the worlds in which we want to live.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Mobilize broad, cross-partisan coalitions to reclaim human attention from extractive digital platforms through a new politics of attention.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within skeptic discourse that advocates for building broad, cross-partisan coalitions to challenge the extractive practices of digital platforms and reclaim human attention. Encompasses: attention activism, cross-partisan mobilization, politics of attention.

key_points.point: The document asserts that digital platforms use 'military-grade technology' to feed children and adults addictive content, causing documented harm to psychological wellbeing and deliberative politics. This 'human fracking' is described as a systematic extraction of attention that treats human consciousness as an unclaimed territory for corporate empire. The authors argue that this is not merely a problem of 'phones' or 'social media,' but a structural issue of how these platforms operate. They note that the damage is already extensive, affecting the very capacity for human care and thought.
key_points.verbatim: The new ôgold rushö into the inner environment of the human psyche is well on its way to e?ecting parallel, if even more insidious destruction.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Digital platforms systematically extract human attention through addictive algorithmic content, causing documented harm to individual wellbeing and democratic processes.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that digital platforms systematically exploit human attention through addictive algorithmic content, resulting in documented harm to individual and societal wellbeing. Encompasses: attention extraction, algorithmic harm, psychological impact.
